title: 44 Evaluating the effects of N-carbamylglutamate and melatonin supplementation in carotid artery hemodynamics and other physiological variables of heat stressed Dorper rams
content:
Abstract
Heat stress negatively affects livestock production by decreasing animal efficiency resulting in economic losses to producers. Melatonin, a neuroendocrine hormone, paired with N-carbamylglutamate, an arginine precursor, could facilitate the production of nitric oxide leading to vasodilation or vasoconstriction in systemic arteries and potentially influence blood redistribution to facilitate heat dissipation. The objective of this study was to evaluate the effect of heat stress and/or dietary supplementation composed of N-carbamylglutamate and melatonin in sheep physiology during a 42 days feedlot period. Twenty-one ram lambs were assigned to 1 of 4 groups consisting of a cooled group with no supplementation (CL-CON; n = 5), a heat stressed group with no supplementation (HS-CON; n = 6), and a cooled or heat stressed group supplemented with 1.4 g/h/d of N-carbamylglutamate and 8mg/h/d of melatonin (CL-NCGMEL, n = 5; HS-NCGMEL n = 5, respectively). Body weight, rectal temperatures, respiration rates, and carotid artery hemodynamics were collected from each individual at day 30 after treatment. Respiration rates and rectal temperatures were collected at 0600 h and 1600 h, thereby, data were analyzed as repeated measurements by the MIXED procedure of SAS and the model included environment, dietary treatment, and time, and their corresponding interactions. No significant differences were found in rectal temperature (P > 0.05), but a significant interaction was observed for respiration rates (P = 0.038) where it was increased in HS-NCGMEL lambs (93 ± 8 bpm) compared to CL-CON (74 ± 9 bpm), HS-CON (73 ± 8 bpm), and CL-NCGMEL animals (63 ± 8 bpm). Doppler ultrasounds of the right carotid artery were performed as an indicator of peripheral blood flow. Data were analyzed by the MIXED procedure of SAS for carotid blood flow and the model included environment, dietary treatment, and their corresponding interactions. A significant difference was observed between dietary treatment groups for carotid artery blood flow (P ≤ 0.05); where the NCGMEL lambs had increased blood flow (425.15 ± 36.27 mL/min) compared to their CON counterparts (330.33 ± 35.18 mL/min). There was no significant difference observed between body weights (P ≥ 0.05), nevertheless, a significant difference was found between dietary treatments for blood flow relative to body weight where it was increased in NCGMEL lambs compared to CON (11.68 ± 1.00 vs. 8.74 ± 0.97 mL/min/kg; P = 0.037). Additionally, the carotid artery diameter was increased in HS lambs compared to their CL counterparts (0.42 ± 0.01 vs. 0.38 ± 0.02 cm; P = 0.02). The significant increase in carotid blood flow for animals supplemented with N-carbamylglutamate and melatonin may indicate a response to facilitating heat dissipation, aiding in blood redistribution to the periphery, thus having the potential to mitigate heat stress in sheep production.
